author: reek
body: A unit is erased at codegen, so `lower-bin-op` has to dispatch on what is inside the wrapper. It stripped nothing, so `UnitTy(RealTy)` matched none of the floating arms and fell through to `IrAddInt`: `Metre 1.5 + Metre 2.5` emitted an INTEGER add of two IEEE-754 bit patterns and returned 9222246136947933184, which is exactly bits(1.5) + bits(2.5).

author: reek
body: This was wrong on EVERY input, not on a quarter of the operand plane like the ordering defect beside it, and it emitted no diagnostic. `CDX9010` guards the comparison emitter; arithmetic never reaches it. The companion `unit-real-compare` covers the ordering half.

author: reek
body: `Tick` is the control, and it is why the hole survived: `unit Integer` wants `IrAddInt` anyway, so it was right by accident. A test written over the obvious unit type would have passed against the broken compiler.

author: reek
body: `Span` wraps `Metre`, which already wraps `Real`. Stripping has to recurse to reach the `Real`, and three of the four unit-stripping predicates in the compiler used to stop after one level. This arm is what holds the recursion.

author: reek
body: Bits, not a rendered decimal: a decimal render cannot show a wrong low mantissa, and the integer-add answer differs so wildly that only an exact comparison states what happened.
